name: The Mazebound Grove
status: Active hazard; Do not enter without earplugs
summary: The Mazebound Grove is a petrified hedge maze on the grounds of the Shadow Estate. It features dead flora, fountains filled with warm blood, and a giant skull-tree draped in corpses. It is also infested with the Mazebound—undead groundskeepers who ambush intruders with coordinated musical numbers. Waluigi would burn this place to ash on principle.
description:
If the Overgrown Manor in the Feywild is nature asserting its dominance, the Mazebound Grove is nature that has been murdered, taxidermied, and forced to perform for aristocratic vampires. 

**The Architecture of Despair**
The maze is constructed of grey trees and hedges with leaves like ash and branches like coal. The thorns curve like raptor talons. In the corners of the maze sit four abandoned fountains brimming with warm, viscous blood that stinks of rich iron. It is impossible to tell where the blood comes from, but there are bloody handprints all over the stone. Waluigi considers this the absolute pinnacle of tasteless vampire décor. It lacks subtlety.

At the heart of the grove stands a towering, dead tree. Its trunk is twisted into the shape of a massive skull with hateful glowing eyes. From its vast branches hang dozens of corpses by the neck, and the boughs are covered in shadow crows with crimson eyes that mock anyone who approaches. Ragged stone obelisks jut from the earth, marked with sigils that cause physical nausea if looked at for too long.

**The Mazebound**
The maze is maintained—and defended—by the Mazebound. These are hunched, snub-nosed humanoids with grey skin, glowing white eyes, and long, scraping nails. They operate with a hive-mind theatricality, speaking in unison, rhyming, and performing synchronized movements before attempting to tear intruders limb from limb. 

Waluigi has navigated many mazes. He has outrun boulders, dodged fireballs, and solved sliding block puzzles. But navigating a maze where the walls literally jump out, do jazz hands, and sing in falsetto about your impending death is a psychological torture that Waluigi refuses to endure. 

There is a small, ancient shrine hidden in the easternmost corner—a statue of a man with a deer's legs and head, holding a barbed spear. Around this shrine, colors return to normal and a sensation of wellness hangs in the air. This is the only safe place in the entire grove, assuming you can survive the musical numbers long enough to find it.

Four fountains continuously overflowing with warm blood
The Skull Tree (draped in corpses and mocking crows)
The Mazebound (singing undead ambushers)
Hidden sanctuary shrine of the Deer-Man

population: Orangus Cornelius (wounded), Kryn Corvinarus (injured), guards of varying loyalty, hostile ghosts, singing servants, Usk, Lyranth, Vaxillus, Mystic Morel, Tanukiburt, the injured real Toadburt, and Disaster Inc. members attempting to leave with all four portal artifacts

status: Active crisis — all four portal artifacts secured by the party, Mirror of True Reflection restored, master-bedroom portal circle occupied, rooftop pursuit spilling onto the grounds
summary:
The Shadow Estate is the Shadowfell's reflection of Raventree Manor—same architecture, same layout, but drained of color, warmth, and anything resembling hospitality. It's controlled by the Onyx Hand's vampiric court, which is CURRENTLY in the middle of a violent succession crisis because Green T shot the lord with a silver bullet and now the heir claimant is hunting party members through maintenance corridors with death magic. The estate has a library, an infirmary, guard patrols, a groundskeeper who grows NORMAL VEGETABLES in a death dimension, and an Archivist who is slowly healing Toadburt in exchange for indentured labor. Waluigi was not sent to the Shadowfell during the Planar Fracture and considers this the ONLY lucky thing that has happened to him during the entire crisis.

Recent update: the estate’s immediate crisis has shifted to the master-bedroom portal circle. The party recovered and mended the Mirror of True Reflection, completing the four-artifact set needed for the Midnight Fountain route, but Remi confirmed Tanukiburt, the injured real Toadburt, and Mystic Morel gathered at the portal circle while Lyranth and Vaxillus pursued the party from below to roof.
description:
Waluigi is documenting the Shadow Estate based on reports from Markop, Bowser, Archie, and Green T—all of whom have spent time inside this place and all of whom describe it with the enthusiasm of people reviewing a hotel they'd give NEGATIVE stars.

## Architecture and Atmosphere

The Shadow Estate mirrors Raventree Manor's physical layout—same corridors, same rooms, same general structure. But everything is WRONG in the specific way the Shadowfell makes things wrong. Before the Shadow Anchor was destroyed, the entire estate existed in monochrome—greys, blacks, the absence of color as an architectural statement. Light didn't illuminate; it just made the darkness MORE visible.

Since Green T shattered the Shadow Anchor during the dinner party climax, color has bled back into parts of the estate. Reds, oranges, yellows—returning violently, making the gothic architecture look, in Waluigi's opinion, incredibly tacky. Like someone painted a funeral home in carnival colors. The restoration of color also restored magical capabilities that the Anchor had suppressed, which was GOOD for Archie (fire works again) and BAD for everyone else (Vivian's crimson death beam also works).

The air presses DOWN in the Shadow Estate. Not metaphorically—the dimension itself exerts a kind of spiritual gravity that makes living visitors feel flattened. Breathing works but feels like effort. Movement works but feels like resistance. The Shadowfell doesn't want you here, and it expresses this through atmospheric oppression.

## The Dining Hall

The most infamous room in the estate—where Orangus Cornelius hosted the dinner party, where guests voted on who would die, where Archie cut off Usk's finger for loyalty points, and where Green T shot the lord through a window with a silver bullet while sitting at the CHILDREN'S TABLE.

The dining hall's windows are shattered from Bowser tackling Cornelius through them. The table still bears marks from being flipped. Blood-wax from vampire candles has hardened on surfaces nobody has cleaned. The room is a crime scene that the estate's staff has apparently decided to leave as-is, either out of respect for history or because nobody wants to clean up after a vampire assassination attempt.

## The Maintenance Corridors

This is where Vivian ambushed Markop and Bowser. The maintenance areas were designed for groundskeepers and servants—utilitarian corridors connecting the estate's functional spaces. Gardening tools, storage rooms, service passages.

One detail that struck Waluigi from Markop's report: a maintenance room contained NORMAL VEGETABLES. Ordinary produce growing under a dim lantern. Not shadow-formed. Not entropy-touched. Just... vegetables. Carrots and whatever else vampires apparently cultivate.

In a dimension of death, someone is growing FOOD. This means the Shadow Estate is more than a vampire court—it's a functioning household. There are groundskeepers who tend gardens. There are routines. There is AGRICULTURE in a death dimension. Waluigi finds this simultaneously comforting and deeply weird. The Shadow Estate has a HR department and a vegetable garden. Even entropy has middle management.

## The Library

The estate maintains a library where Toadburt was found speaking with Pierce Anamatar. The library appears to be a functional repository of knowledge—books, records, possibly Corvinarus family documents. The Archivist operates from somewhere connected to this space.

Remi discovered the library during her exploration and found imps struggling to organize fallen bookshelves. She helped them clean up in exchange for reconnaissance—a transaction that Waluigi respects because it demonstrates PRACTICAL diplomacy. You don't need fancy speeches when you can trade shelf-lifting for information.

## The Infirmary

The Shadow Estate has medical facilities staffed by attendants who examine visitors with professional competence and suspicious thoroughness. After Remi's glowing potion incident, guards carried her to the infirmary for examination.

The infirmary staff proposed placing an entropy-blocking ring on Remi—the same type of obedience device the Iron Legion strapped on Toadburt. The stated reason was 'preventing outside magical interference while evaluating potion effects.' The ACTUAL reason, Waluigi suspects, is that the Shadow Estate's management wants to CONTROL anyone displaying unusual magical phenomena within their domain.

Entropy rings are OBEDIENCE COLLARS. Waluigi has documented this position repeatedly. Any institution that proposes putting one on a party member should be treated with extreme suspicion regardless of their stated medical justifications.

## Guard Presence

The Shadow Estate maintains a significant guard force that patrols corridors, monitors visitors, and enforces the estate's rules. The guards are caught in an uncomfortable position during the succession crisis—technically serving Orangus Cornelius, but facing a situation where the heir claimant is actively hunting people through the corridors they patrol.

Guard backgrounds vary widely. When Remi questioned several guards about their origins and recruitment, the answers were inconsistent—different backgrounds, different timelines, different stories. This suggests the guard force is assembled from diverse sources rather than a unified military tradition. Some may be thralls. Some may be independent contractors. Some may be playing both sides of the succession.

A purple toad among the guards was responsible for giving Remi the glowing potion and later offered her a fae-style bargain trading mental perception for a promise of passage home. He was subsequently detained by Shadowfell guards for performing unauthorized magic within the estate. Even the VAMPIRES considered his deal inappropriate.

## The Archivist

The Archivist is a figure Waluigi knows little about but finds CONCERNING. This individual operates within the estate's knowledge infrastructure and has taken Toadburt under a healing arrangement: gradual recovery over two-week intervals in exchange for archival work.

This is indentured service dressed up as medical care. Toadburt's entropy ring has been removed—he's no longer the Iron Legion's leashed agent—but he's traded one form of bondage for another. The Iron Legion controlled him through a device. The Archivist controls him through need. The mechanism is different. The loss of autonomy is similar.

Waluigi doesn't know the Archivist's agenda. Someone who runs a knowledge repository in a vampire estate during a succession crisis has access to INFORMATION, and information is power. Whether the Archivist serves Orangus, supports Vivian, or pursues independent objectives remains unclear.

## Waluigi's Assessment

The Shadow Estate is not just a haunted house. It's a FUNCTIONING INSTITUTION with gardens, guards, libraries, infirmaries, administrative staff, and an Archivist who trades healing for labor. It has entropy rings for visitors and vegetable gardens for... Waluigi doesn't actually know who eats the vegetables. Vampires don't eat vegetables. The thralls? The groundskeepers? The imps?

The point is: the Shadow Estate is MORE organized than it initially appeared, and that organization makes it MORE dangerous, not less. Disorganized threats can be navigated through chaos. Organized threats have SYSTEMS, and systems are hard to escape.

With Vivian actively hunting through corridors he mapped during weeks as a thrall, Orangus wounded and recovery uncertain, guards of divided loyalty, and the infirmary trying to ring party members with obedience devices, the Shadow Estate has become a pressure cooker.

Waluigi is glad he's in the Feywild. The fairy riddles are ANNOYING but at least the fairies don't chase him through maintenance corridors with death beams.

WAH.

## Usk’s Chambers, the Master Bedroom Portal Circle, and the Roof

The Mirror of True Reflection was recovered from Usk’s private chambers after the ghost complained about people touching his stuff and revealed the mirror had been broken. Remi restored the mirror with Mending after the missing piece was found. The master bedroom portal circle is now the most important tactical point in the estate: Tanukiburt, the injured real Toadburt, and Mystic Morel were seen gathered around it. The rooftop became an escape route and then a trap as Lyranth, Vaxillus, ghosts, and guards converged. Remi’s Feather Fall evacuation moved the party from the roof to the grounds, but did not solve the occupied-exit problem.

Featuring a deer-headed statue with glowing orange eyes, it is said to hold the memories of the grounds that the vampire lords have forgotten. description:
Waluigi is documenting this shrine because it represents a 'Class-A Anomaly' in the Shadowfell's entropic field. 

## The Statue of the Orange Eyes
The centerpiece of the shrine is a weathered statue of a deer-headed figure. Unlike the rest of the Shadowfell, the statue's eyes glow with a soft, warm orange light—matching the color of the 'spark' associated with Archie Miser. This light does not fade, and it appears to resist the surrounding monochrome decay.

## The Path of Color
According to cryptic reports, reaching the shrine without 'listening too long to the songs' allows a traveler to see paths that are invisible to the entropic eye. It is a place of 'Administrative Sanctuary,' where the rules of the Shadowfell are suspended in favor of the 'Old Fires.'

## Waluigi's Assessment
A shrine that holds color in a world of grey is either a miracle or a very high-quality trap. Waluigi suspects it is an anchor for the 'Old World' energy that the Iron Legion is so desperate to catalog. If the statue is watching, Waluigi wants to know who is looking through its eyes. WAH.

Despite existing in the color-draining ash wastes of the Shadowfell, the cottage retains rich yellow and green interiors and hearth warmth that resist entropy. It has repeatedly served as Disaster Inc.'s primary safehouse and defensive bunker, most notably during the 29 Harvestide Imp Ambush, the Harvestide 28 Midnight Audit, and the Cookie Cottage spotlight chase. The latest night filing adds a failed lockdown: Remi and Markop sealed the cottage against an unnatural storm and an uninvited vampire, only for an imp discovered in the broom closet to grant the vampire permission to enter. Dan's Holy Symbol of Ravenkind burned half the intruder's face away, Wario smashed another window on arrival, and Markop converted a closet door into an emergency shutter.
description:
# TYMNAS'S COTTAGE & THE SHADOW ESTATE HEDGE MAZE
### Definitive Architectural, Botanical, and Tactical Siege Survey
### Filed by Waluigi, Auditor-General of Planar Real Estate and Custodial Defense

Waluigi has audited palaces, fortresses, mountain tombs, and floating gambling establishments, but no single residential property in the known multiverse has experienced as many sieges, midnight thievery audits, spotlight escapes, and insect home-invasions as **Tymnas the Groundskeeper's Cottage**. Nestled inside the labyrinthine gray foliage of the Shadow Estate Hedge Maze at the periphery of Raventree Manor, this modest one-story stone cottage is an anomalous miracle of planar real estate.

In a dimension where entropic forces suck the color out of clothing, turn skin ash-gray, and transform family reunions into crimson-beam executions, Tymnas's cottage stubbornly remains warm, well-insulated, and bursting with vibrant yellows and greens. It is the only structure on the estate where a party member can sit on clean floorboards without an ancient vampire staring through the keyhole—which is precisely why Disaster Inc. has turned it into their permanent frontline command bunker. WAH!

---

## 1. Architectural Layout & The Chromatic Anomaly of the Shadowfell

### The Chromatic Preservation Phenomenon
To understand why Tymnas's cottage is so tactically vital, one must examine its metaphysical insulation. Throughout Raventree Manor, ambient Shadowfell entropy degrades color and emotion. Yet within Tymnas's stone walls, colors glimmer with intense richness. Waluigi's investigation reveals that this is not accidental: Tymnas has cultivated a surrounding buffer of gray topiary that absorbs entropic decay, while the tall timber chimney burns cured aromatic cedar and swamp-herbs that create a positive magical interior pressure. 

When Markop's equine eyes snap open at dawn, the rich yellows and greens of the cottage interior actively strain against the gray twilight pressing against the window panes. It is, in Waluigi's professional assessment, a pressurized bubble of domestic sanity in a dimension of Gothic lunacy.

### Complete Floor Plan & Defensive Anatomy
The cottage is structured for efficiency, custodial storage, and defensibility:
- **The Stone Bedroom & Lead-Paned Windows**: Located on the eastern wall, featuring low straw bedding specially proportioned for Markop's four-legged horse frame. The leaded glass window overlooks the tangled hedge treeline and was the site of the infamous 29 Harvestide window-tapping by the armored imp.
- **The Central Kitchen & Dining Parlor**: Dominated by a heavy, circular timber dining table where Tymnas serves herbal tea and where wounded defenders collapse during sieges. It was upon this very table that the Archivist's right-hand imp fell after being sliced in half by Markop, whispering *"Tell my wife I love her..."*
- **The Washroom & Bathroom Window**: A compact washroom with a cast-iron bathtub and a narrow rear ventilation window. This room served as Remi Akamatsu's testing ground for the Black Crystal lie detector during the Harvestide 28 Midnight Audit, and later became the scene of a near-fatal tactical breach when invisible imps infiltrated the window and drenched Remi in heavy toxic poison from behind.
- **The Front Threshold & Porch**: A heavy timber door reinforced with iron straps and flanked by Tymnas's groundskeeping tool racks. It is the primary choke-point for defending against manor intrusions, and the location of the chilling **Phantom Knock** that opened to empty, swirling gray fog.

---

## 2. The Labyrinthine Hedge Maze & Botanical Entrapment

Surrounding the cottage is the **Shadow Estate Hedge Maze**, an expansive, overgrown labyrinth of ash-colored topiary, thorny briers, and shifting pathways that separates Raventree Manor's formal gardens from the swampy wastes.

### Entropic Botany & Amnesia Vines
The flora of the Hedge Maze is semi-sentient and responds to emotional distress. Foliage shifts shape when unobserved, closing off retreat routes and guiding trespassers toward central snares. Certain species of vines display amnesia-adjacent hazards similar to the Feyward overgrown zones, capable of wiping short-term spatial memory from intruders who linger too long in the mist.

### Groundskeeper Wards & Tool Networks
Tymnas maintains absolute mastery over the maze's paths. By deploying scented candle alarms, tripwire snares, and herbal smudges, he can detect invisible or shifting planar creatures before they reach the cottage porch. His tool network has historically supplied Disaster Inc. with practical problem-solving hardware—most famously the **Trowel of Retrieving**, which Markop used to promote a stuck window into an emergency escape route during the spotlight pursuit.

---

## 3. Historical Record of Party Occupations & Recurring Sieges

Why has this humble groundskeeper's homestead become the most contested piece of property in 1040 BF? Because Disaster Inc. cannot stop retreating into it!
- **The Harvestide 14 Cookie Cottage Spotlight Chase**: Following the Vostolas servant-corridor artifact chain and the acquisition of the Black Crystal, the party fled through the hedge maze under the glare of Corvinarus searchlights, taking refuge in Tymnas's cottage to consolidate their stolen loot.
- **The Harvestide 28 Midnight Audit**: Intruders breached the cottage perimeter while Remi Akamatsu was testing the Black Crystal's resonance. Remi de-escalated the intruders, reclaimed her stolen firearm, and discovered a cloaked spy hiding in Tymnas's bedroom clothing closet.
- **The Harvestide 29 Imp Ambush**: The definitive siege of the cottage, where an army of imps representing the deceased Archivist surrounded the homestead to reclaim their stolen ledger.

---

## 4. The Harvestide 29 Imp Ambush: Complete Tactical Siege Audit

On Harvestide 29, 1040 BF, the cottage underwent its most violent operational test. Waluigi has reconstructed the five distinct phases of the defense from Markop and Remi's field logs:

### Phase I: The Dawn Window Tap & The Pacifist Debate
At dawn, Markop was awakened by a rhythmic *tap, tap, tap* on the bedroom window. Outside hovered a miniature imp in rusted chainmail armor. When the imp accused Markop of murdering the Archivist, Markop argued *"Self-defense,"* pointing out that an archivist who threatens to erase a person's entire genetic lineage from existence is not a pacifist. The imp demanded the return of the library ledger or threatened an immediate assault by his nine-man army.

### Phase II: The Frontal Charge & Dan's Multi-Dimensional Sentry Eye
Markop alerted the sleeping Remi Akamatsu, armed Tymnas with a short sword, and rallied Eager, Salam, and Rattles at the front door. Parallel Dan opened his special multi-dimensional sensory eye, piercing the imps' invisibility cloaking and directing Eager's high-speed slashing attacks. Salam executed a crucial backstab on an advancing imp, while Rattles held the window flank.

### Phase III: The Bathroom Window Breach & Poisoning of Remi
Realizing the front door was impenetrable, a strike team of invisible imps bypassed the porch and infiltrated the washroom window. Remi Akamatsu, isolated in the bathroom, was ambushed from behind and drenched in a heavy, burning toxic poison. Despite severe agony, Remi retaliated with dual crossbow shots, alerting Markop to the rear breach.

### Phase IV: The Kitchen Melee & The Right-Hand Man's Fall
Markop rushed into the kitchen dining parlor, swinging his battleaxe in a sweeping arc that sliced the Archivist's second-in-command in half across Tymnas's dining table. As the dying imp wheezed, *"Tell my wife I love her..."*, the remaining intruders broke formation and fled into the hedge maze.

### Phase V: The Phantom Knock at the Threshold
In the aftermath of the melee, with Remi poisoned and Tymnas guarding the window, a slow, heavy knock echoed at the front door: *Knock. Knock. Knock.* When Markop creaked the door wide, the porch was completely empty—nothing stood outside except the swirling, ash-colored fog of the Shadowfell. Whether an illusion, an invisible Corvinarus assassin, or a warning from the estate itself, the cottage remains an active war zone.

---

## 5. Waluigi's Geopolitical & Real Estate Verdict

Waluigi's assessment of Tymnas's Cottage is unequivocal:
1. **Strategic Value**: It is the single most valuable defensible safehouse in the Shadowfell, providing chromatic and thermal protection against ambient entropic decay.
2. **Vulnerability**: The bathroom rear window is a severe tactical liability that Tymnas must immediately reinforce with iron bars or phase-spider webbing.
3. **The Groundskeeper's Loyalty**: Tymnas is the most competent groundskeeper in the Regal Empire, providing weapons, snares, and tea to a group of wanted fugitives without ever once asking for a 2,000-gold rope deposit.

Waluigi recommends that Disaster Inc. pay Tymnas a permanent retainer—or at least stop inviting armored flying insects to his breakfast table! WAH!

name: Shadow Estate Gardens
summary: The Shadow Estate Gardens, once a sanctuary of peace and beauty, now stand as a testament to the fragility of harmony in Dreamland.
description: **The Shadow Estate Gardens** In the heart of the verdant rolling hills of Dreamland, nestled between the whispering branches and the rustling leaves, stood the once-majestic Shadow Estate Gardens. It was a place where time seemed to slow down, its tranquility a balm for weary souls. The gardens were not just a collection of plants; they were a living testament to the harmonious balance that existed in Dreamland before discord crept into the fabric of its existence. The estate itself had been built by Sir Cedric Darkshade, a man whose name once evoked admiration and respect among the inhabitants of Dreamland. His vision was to create a garden that would be a symbol of peace and beauty, a place where all could find solace and escape from the stresses of daily life. The gardens were designed with an intricate blend of natural elements—water cascading over stone fountains, meandering paths lined with vibrant flowers, and grand trees that offered shade to those seeking respite. The entrance was guarded by two colossal statues of mythical creatures, their eyes gleaming with a mysterious light that seemed almost alive. Beyond this entrance lay a labyrinthine pathway paved with smooth, black cobblestones, leading visitors deeper into the garden's secrets. Each step down this path brought one closer to the heart of the estate where a grand pond reflected the sky above. Sir Cedric's dedication was evident in every detail. He employed the best horticulturists and artists of his time who worked tirelessly to bring his vision to life. The gardens were divided into distinct sections, each dedicated to different flora from around Dreamland, showcasing the diversity that made the country so unique. There were lush green lawns where children would play under the watchful eyes of their parents; secret nooks filled with fragrant herbs and wildflowers; and serene corners where lovers could find privacy amidst nature's embrace. The centerpiece of the estate was a vast greenhouse, its glass roof allowing sunlight to filter through in just the right way. Inside, exotic plants thrived regardless of the seasons outside. It was here that Sir Cedric conducted his experiments in botany, pushing the boundaries of what was possible with plant life. He believed strongly in the power of nature and sought ways to enhance it for everyone's benefit. As years passed, the estate became more than just a garden; it evolved into a center for intellectual discourse and cultural exchange. Scholars from far and wide would gather here, sharing ideas and fostering new understandings that contributed positively to society. It was during these gatherings that Sir Cedric first proposed his theories about maintaining balance through harmony with nature. His philosophy suggested that by understanding our relationship with the natural world, we could create a more harmonious existence for all beings. The gardens were not merely a place of rest; they were also used as an educational tool. Young students from various schools would visit regularly to learn about botany and horticulture under the guidance of experienced gardeners. They learned about the importance of sustainability in maintaining ecosystems, how different plants interacted with each other, and the impact human activities could have on these interactions. Despite its initial success, the Shadow Estate Gardens faced challenges. The growing tensions between various factions within Dreamland began to affect even this idyllic place. As political strife increased, visitors became fewer and the estate's resources stretched thin. Despite these difficulties, Sir Cedric remained steadfast in his dedication to preserving the gardens' beauty and purpose. Tragedy struck when a violent storm swept through Dreamland, damaging sections of the garden beyond repair. The community rallied together, but it was not enough to save everything. Some parts of the estate were abandoned as funds dwindled and resources became scarce. Over time, weeds began to overtake neglected areas, and once-pristine pathways became overgrown with vines. Today, the Shadow Estate Gardens stands as a poignant reminder of better days gone by. Though much has been lost, there remains a strong desire among the people of Dreamland to restore this cherished site. Efforts are ongoing to preserve what can be saved and replant where possible. Volunteers work tirelessly under the direction of modern horticulturists who seek to honor Sir Cedric's legacy. Visitors today find themselves in a place that is both familiar yet altered—some areas lush with greenery while others lie barren. It evokes a sense of nostalgia and hope, symbolizing not only what was lost but also the potential for renewal. The gardens serve as a living museum where past meets present, inviting contemplation on themes of harmony, resilience, and sustainability. In recent times, there has been renewed interest in restoring parts of the garden. Local artists have contributed to this effort by painting murals depicting scenes from its golden era along the walls surrounding it. These artworks add color and life back into spaces that were once darkened by neglect or destruction. Visitors can now walk through sections adorned with vibrant imagery, bringing back some of the joy and wonder that made visiting these grounds so special in previous generations. Despite all that has changed since those halcyon days when the estate thrived as a beacon of peace and beauty, the essence remains intact. The gardens continue to offer solace to many who seek refuge from modern concerns. They remind us all about the importance of nurturing relationships with nature, respecting our environment, and working together towards common goals—lessons that remain relevant even today. The Shadow Estate Gardens, now standing as a symbol of resilience against adversity, continues to inspire hope within Dreamland's citizens. Its story serves as both a cautionary tale and an invitation for future generations to learn from history and build upon its lessons. Herein lies the enduring power of this place—a testament to the enduring spirit of those who once called it home.

summary: The Skittering Grove is what is inside the Scorncrow's tree — and it is the Silent Grove, the same web-choked forest the party cleared after banishing the Arachnid Matriarch. Markop recognised it on arrival and walked to the stump they had stacked the loot on. You reach it by rope, through the tree's jaws, down a pit that a thrown torch does not measure. The archive now holds one grove with two entrances: a walk across Raventree Manor's grounds, and a scarecrow's mouth in the Shadowfell.
description:
Markop recognised it before anyone else did, and what he recognised is the whole entry: this is the Silent Grove. The party cleared it. They are standing in it again, inside something that was growing in a field an hour ago.

**The Approach**
There is no door. There is a mouth. When Markop pried the jaws of the trunk open he saw darkness first and a giant pit second, in that order, which is the order things arrive in here. The party threw a torch in as a test. The torch came back out of the trunk — and on the inside, Remi heard voices saying *there's a fire, someone's causing a fire, they're going to burn us all down*. That is the whole location in one exchange: you cannot sound it, and something in it is talking about you.

**The Heart**
At the centre stands a great, towering tree with vast branches reaching out to form a canopy over the area. Its boughs are coated in thick webs that are an unnerving mockery of foliage, and hanging from them are the forms of wrapped creatures, both beast and man, dangling like macabre fruit. The tree is long dead — some terrible malady killed it from the inside out years ago. Its dark roots jut from grey earth that no longer nourishes it, and its great arms serve as home to an unimaginable host of creeping, crawling arachnids that accost anything which wanders into their domain.

**What Lives Here**
Giant green spiders that fight with webs before they fight with fangs. Ettercaps that reel their targets in on a strand and open with a multiattack. And — filed with the discomfort it deserves — Legion soldiers, inside, alongside the brood, on ground no Legion column marched to.

**Fire**
Archie's fire bolt scarred the bark and did nothing else. Fire magic is weakened in this domain, which the wizard tested twice before believing it and then answered by emptying every reserve he had into a single cast. The tree took it. The exit did not survive.

**It Is the Silent Grove**
It is not a second one. Markop recognised it on arrival and named it: this is the Silent Grove, the web-choked forest on Raventree Manor's northwestern boundary where the party banished the Arachnid Matriarch. Same great dead tree, same web canopy, same grey earth. He walked to the broad flat stump at the roots — the stump the loot was stacked on that night, the War Mage's Staff he claimed on Archie's behalf, the Web-Woven Scale, the three healing potions — put a hand on it, and said so out loud. Nobody else in the party recognised it.

**Waluigi's Assessment**
So the archive is holding two facts that do not fit in the same box. The Silent Grove is on Raventree Manor's grounds and you reach it by walking. The Silent Grove is also inside the Scorncrow's tree and you reach it by rope, through a mouth, in the Shadowfell. Both are filed. Both are attested. Waluigi is not going to pretend that a place he helped clear has stayed cleared, or stayed put, and the open question is not whether this grove moved — it is whether it was ever only in one place. The Legion are standing in it. Somebody should ask how they walk there. WAH.

summary: The room the party stumbled into while running from the brood. It is Pierce Anamatar's holding, it is staffed with his knights, and it sits inside ground the Mages' Guild claims — a fact Anamatar raises himself, and volunteers that he does not like the Guild. Passage out is available. It is not free.
description:
Waluigi files this as a location rather than a scene because a room where somebody sets prices is a place of business.

Wario came in punching and found nothing to punch. The room was already occupied: wrights standing in the dark, and then Anamatar himself, arriving to ask why a stranger was fighting his people in his den.

What followed was a negotiation conducted between a man who was frightened and a man who enjoyed that. Wario said he was running from the spiders. Anamatar asked whether he was afraid of a few creepy-crawlies and offered him a bandaid and a sippy cup. Wario said yes, he was, and asked whether Anamatar had seen what they look like.

Then the terms. This is Guild-controlled ground; Anamatar does not like the Guild; he will send them back where they came from **in exchange for something of theirs**. He asked first for the siglet — the ring the party has been chasing since Tymnas's lodge — and settled for [Remi's](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/remi_akamatsu_full_backstory) student ID card, on the grounds that it is very durable.

Waluigi notes the shape of the deal and not its size. The man did not want money. He wanted a **thing that belongs to somebody**, and he took the one piece of paper in the grove that proves a fourteen-year-old was ever enrolled anywhere.

An expired coupon was offered and declined
